title: Choose the visual world for the AI Insights dashboard
question: The roll assigned the Consumption Statement. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Consumption Statement
options.thesis: The assistant is metered like a utility: this period against the last, priced with your own tariff.
options.viewport: Ultramarine rail, a statement summary (cost, turns, users) with paired this-vs-last bars, then itemised turns.
options.risk: Reads as an invoice if the paired bars and tariff are not doing real work on every page.

raised.raise: Figures sit in fixed tabular cells; columns never shift when values change.
A conversation is drawn as one ordered line whose stops are model calls, searches and tool calls.
Each page leads with one plain-language answer before any metric.
Hairline module grid packs twice the rows a SaaS card layout would.
Every period chart shares one scale and baseline, so pages compare at a glance.

options.label: Itemised Phone Bill
options.thesis: Every turn is a call on the bill: time, duration, units, cost, one line each.
options.viewport: Summary box with totals by category, then the call-by-call listing grouped by day.
options.risk: Familiar and table-heavy; the listing can drown the charts a product owner needs.

options.label: Gate Board and Boarding Pass
options.lineage: airport departure boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: Conversations rank like departures; each turn opens as a segmented pass.
options.viewport: A ranked board of recent turns with status columns; KPIs as pass segments above it.
options.case: Holds product clarity with ranked live rows; loses audience identification, since cost and consumption are the product owner's language.
options.risk: Ranking by time hides period comparison, the core weekly question.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Service health as a coloured line network.
options.viewport: A network map of tools and stores.
options.case: Only the conversation view maps to a line; the period pages do not.
options.risk: A map costume on a numbers screen.
options.kept: A conversation as one ordered line with stops.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Live turns flip in like departures.
options.case: Animation competes with reading; weekly review is not a live concourse.
options.kept: Fixed tabular cells that never shift.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One conversation fills the screen at a time.
options.case: Loses comparison and density, the two things the dashboard is for.
options.kept: One headline answer leads each page.

options.label: Japanese High-Density Web
options.thesis: Pack every module onto one scroll.
options.case: Identification is weak for this audience; clarity drops at that density.
options.kept: Hairline module discipline and density courage.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Periods as plates on one baseline.
options.viewport: Five period plates side by side.
options.case: No audience link to botanical plates; cream ground is a known rut.
options.kept: One shared scale for every period chart.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: An observability dashboard as Grafana or Datadog ship it, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: KPI cards in a row, line charts below, a table of recent turns.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dashboard by design.
